description: Post-COVID, B1/B2 waits in Mexico reached nearly three years. By mid-2023 Ciudad Juárez and Guadalajara were showing first availability only in 2025.
energy_note: Apply now, be seen the year after next.

aspect: It recovered unevenly and is still long
description: By June 2025 the Mexico City average had dropped below 200 days, with Monterrey and Tijuana shorter in some weeks; other guidance still cited 300+ days into late 2025. Peak months are November-January and June-August.
energy_note: Better, and still most of a year.

aspect: The wait prices out the emergency
description: A funeral, a sick parent, a daughter's graduation, a contract that starts in March - none of these can wait 300 days, so the visa system is structurally unable to serve the reasons people most want to travel.
energy_note: By the time it comes through, the reason is over.

aspect: Consulate towns run on the queue
description: Ciudad Juárez has an economy built around people waiting: hotels, photo shops, form-fillers, notarios, medical exam clinics. The applicant pays all of it before he knows the answer.
energy_note: A whole town charging him while he waits to be refused.
